Detection Script Content
View script
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Detects the requested Windows language configuration for Intune Remediations.
.DESCRIPTION
    Reads the current device state directly and verifies the device completion
    receipt that releases paired user-context policies. An already-correct
    device without the receipt triggers one remediation run that adopts it by
    recording the receipt without reinstalling anything.
.NOTES
    Product: Language Pack Deployer
    Version: 1.0.0

    Exit codes:
      0    The requested device configuration is present
      1    Remediation is required or detection failed

    Detection runs in device context. Settings that belong to an interactive
    user profile, such as keyboard preferences and user culture, are not tested.

    Restart required: Windows reports some device settings - notably the
    system locale - with their old values until the device restarts. A freshly
    remediated device can therefore stay non-compliant here, and remediation
    can run again (harmlessly, it is idempotent), until a restart.
#>

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# <LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>
$tags = @('en-US')
$primaryTag = 'en-US'
$timezone = 'W. Europe Standard Time'
$configurationId = 'cfg-v1-eb1ac170'
# </LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>

try {
    $installedLanguages = @(Get-InstalledLanguage)
    $issues = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

    Write-Output 'Language Pack Deployer - Device detection'
    Write-Output "Requested languages: $($tags -join ', ')"
    Write-Output "Primary language: $primaryTag"

    foreach ($tag in $tags) {
        if ($installedLanguages.LanguageId -notcontains $tag) {
            $issues.Add("Language pack is not installed: $tag")
            Write-Output "[FAIL] Installed language: $tag"
        }
        else {
            Write-Output "[PASS] Installed language: $tag"
        }
    }

    $actualUiLanguage = Get-SystemPreferredUILanguage
    if ($actualUiLanguage -ne $primaryTag) {
        $issues.Add("System preferred UI language is '$actualUiLanguage'; expected '$primaryTag'")
        Write-Output "[FAIL] System preferred UI language: $actualUiLanguage (expected: $primaryTag)"
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "[PASS] System preferred UI language: $actualUiLanguage"
    }

    $actualSystemLocale = (Get-WinSystemLocale).Name
    if ($actualSystemLocale -ne $primaryTag) {
        $issues.Add("System locale is '$actualSystemLocale'; expected '$primaryTag'")
        Write-Output "[FAIL] System locale: $actualSystemLocale (expected: $primaryTag)"
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "[PASS] System locale: $actualSystemLocale"
    }

    $actualTimezone = (Get-TimeZone).Id
    if ($actualTimezone -ne $timezone) {
        $issues.Add("Timezone is '$actualTimezone'; expected '$timezone'")
        Write-Output "[FAIL] Timezone: $actualTimezone (expected: $timezone)"
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "[PASS] Timezone: $actualTimezone"
    }

    # The device remediation records this receipt when it completes (or adopts
    # an already-correct device). Paired user-context policies wait for it, so
    # a missing or outdated receipt must trigger one remediation run.
    $receipt = Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\LanguagePackDeployer\Remediation' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $receipt -or $receipt.Completed -ne 1 -or $receipt.ConfigurationId -ne $configurationId) {
        $issues.Add('Device completion receipt is missing or belongs to another configuration')
        Write-Output '[FAIL] Device completion receipt: missing or outdated (user policies wait for it)'
    }
    else {
        Write-Output '[PASS] Device completion receipt: present'
    }

    if ($issues.Count -gt 0) {
        Write-Output "Result: Non-compliant ($($issues.Count) issue(s))"
        foreach ($issue in $issues) {
            Write-Output " - $issue"
        }
        exit 1
    }

    Write-Output 'Result: Compliant (all device checks passed)'
    exit 0
}
catch {
    Write-Output "Language configuration detection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit 1
}
Remediation Script Content
View script
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Installs and configures one or more Windows language packs.
.DESCRIPTION
    Ensures that the requested language packs are installed and applies the
    selected primary language and regional settings. Win32 deployments also
    record state for their registry-based Intune detection rules.

    The script is safe to run repeatedly. Existing language packs are reused,
    and settings that are already correct are left unchanged.
.NOTES
    Product:      Language Pack Deployer
    Version:      1.0.0
    Requirements: Windows 11 22H2 or later
                  64-bit Windows PowerShell
                  Administrator or SYSTEM context

    Exit codes:
      0    Success or already configured
      1    Installation or configuration failed
      3010 Success with restart required (Win32 deployments only)

    Intune Remediations and platform scripts always return 0 after a successful
    run, including when a restart or new sign-in is required. This script never
    forces a restart.

    Restart required: Windows reports some device settings - notably the
    system locale - with their old values until the device restarts. A freshly
    remediated device can therefore stay non-compliant in detection, and the
    remediation can run again (harmlessly, it is idempotent), until a restart.
#>

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$registryRoot = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\LanguagePackDeployer'
$templateVersion = '1.0.0'

# <LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>
$languages = @(
    @{ Tag = 'en-US'; GeoId = 244; Timezone = 'W. Europe Standard Time'; Keyboard = '00020409'; KeyboardName = 'US-International' }
)
$primaryTag = 'en-US'
$rebootRequested = $false
$deploymentTarget = 'remediation'
$configurationId = 'cfg-v1-eb1ac170'
# </LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>

# --- 64-bit guard: IME is 32-bit; language modules need 64-bit PowerShell ---
if ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 -eq 'AMD64') {
    $sysnative = "$env:WINDIR\sysnative\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe"
    & $sysnative -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

# --- OS guard: Install-Language requires Windows 11 22H2+ ---
$build = [System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version.Build
if ($build -lt 22621) {
    Write-Output "Unsupported OS build $build - Install-Language requires Windows 11 22H2 (build 22621) or later."
    exit 1
}

if ($deploymentTarget -notin @('win32', 'remediation', 'platformScript')) {
    Write-Output "Unsupported deployment target: $deploymentTarget"
    exit 1
}

function Save-OriginalState {
    # Preserve the original state once so the final uninstall can restore it.
    if (Get-ItemProperty -Path $registryRoot -Name 'OriginalState' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { return }
    $state = @{
        languageList = @((Get-WinUserLanguageList).LanguageTag)
        culture      = (Get-Culture).Name
        geoId        = (Get-WinHomeLocation).GeoId
        timezone     = (Get-TimeZone).Id
        systemLocale = (Get-WinSystemLocale).Name
        systemPreferredLanguage = (Get-SystemPreferredUILanguage)
        capturedAt   = (Get-Date).ToString('o')
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
    New-Item -Path $registryRoot -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $registryRoot -Name 'OriginalState' -Value $state -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
}

function Save-DeploymentMarker([string]$tag) {
    $key = Join-Path (Join-Path $registryRoot 'Deployments') $tag
    New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Installed' -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Version' -Value $templateVersion -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'ConfigurationId' -Value $configurationId -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Timestamp' -Value (Get-Date).ToString('o') -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
}

function Save-RemediationMarker {
    # Completion receipt for the paired user-context policy. User detection and
    # remediation wait for this key before touching any profile, because pack
    # presence alone is a false readiness signal: in a migration the target
    # pack is often already installed while the device settings are not yet
    # configured. The receipt carries the ConfigurationId so a receipt from an
    # older deployment never releases user policies for a newer one.
    $key = Join-Path $registryRoot 'Remediation'
    New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Completed' -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Version' -Value $templateVersion -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'ConfigurationId' -Value $configurationId -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Timestamp' -Value (Get-Date).ToString('o') -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
}

function Get-KeyboardTip([hashtable]$lang) {
    # InputMethodTip format: "<LCID hex>:<KLID>", e.g. 0413:00020409 = Dutch + US-International.
    if (-not $lang.Keyboard) { return $null }
    $lcidHex = '{0:x4}' -f ([System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::GetCultureInfo($lang.Tag).LCID)
    return "${lcidHex}:$($lang.Keyboard)"
}

function Set-KeyboardLayout([hashtable]$lang) {
    $tip = Get-KeyboardTip $lang
    if (-not $tip) { return }
    $list = Get-WinUserLanguageList
    $entry = $list | Where-Object { $_.LanguageTag -eq $lang.Tag }
    if ($entry -and ($entry.InputMethodTips -notcontains $tip)) {
        $entry.InputMethodTips.Clear()
        $entry.InputMethodTips.Add($tip) | Out-Null
        Set-WinUserLanguageList -LanguageList $list -Force
    }
}

function Test-CurrentAccountSettings([hashtable]$lang, [bool]$isPrimary) {
    # Under the recommended SYSTEM context these values are the source copied
    # to the welcome screen and defaults for new users. They do not represent
    # an already signed-in interactive user's profile.
    $list = Get-WinUserLanguageList
    $entry = $list | Where-Object { $_.LanguageTag -eq $lang.Tag }
    if (-not $entry) { return $false }
    $tip = Get-KeyboardTip $lang
    if ($tip -and ($entry.InputMethodTips -notcontains $tip)) { return $false }
    if ($isPrimary) {
        if ((Get-Culture).Name -ne $lang.Tag) { return $false }
        if ((Get-WinHomeLocation).GeoId -ne $lang.GeoId) { return $false }
    }
    return $true
}

try {
    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
        Save-OriginalState
    }

    $installedTags = @((Get-InstalledLanguage).LanguageId)
    $allLanguagesInstalled = $true
    foreach ($lang in $languages) {
        if ($installedTags -notcontains $lang.Tag) { $allLanguagesInstalled = $false }
    }

    $primaryLanguage = $languages | Where-Object { $_.Tag -eq $primaryTag }
    $deviceSettingsConfigured = (
        (Get-SystemPreferredUILanguage) -eq $primaryTag -and
        (Get-WinSystemLocale).Name -eq $primaryTag -and
        (Get-TimeZone).Id -eq $primaryLanguage.Timezone
    )
    $currentAccountSettingsConfigured = $true
    foreach ($lang in $languages) {
        if (-not (Test-CurrentAccountSettings $lang ($lang.Tag -eq $primaryTag))) {
            $currentAccountSettingsConfigured = $false
        }
    }
    $allSettingsConfigured = $deviceSettingsConfigured -and $currentAccountSettingsConfigured

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
        Write-Output 'Language Pack Deployer - Device remediation'
        Write-Output "Requested languages: $(($languages.Tag) -join ', ')"
        Write-Output "Primary language: $primaryTag"
        Write-Output "Timezone: $($primaryLanguage.Timezone)"
        foreach ($lang in $languages) {
            if ($installedTags -contains $lang.Tag) {
                Write-Output "[PASS] Language pack already installed: $($lang.Tag)"
            }
            else {
                Write-Output "[ACTION] Language pack requires installation: $($lang.Tag)"
            }
        }
    }

    if ($deploymentTarget -ne 'win32' -and $allLanguagesInstalled -and $allSettingsConfigured) {
        # Adopt an already-correct device: record the completion receipt so the
        # paired user-context policy is released without reinstalling anything.
        Save-RemediationMarker
        if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
            Write-Output '[APPLIED] Device completion receipt recorded for user policies'
            Write-Output 'Result: Compliant (no remediation changes were required)'
        }
        else {
            Write-Output 'Language pack(s) and device settings are already configured. No changes made.'
        }
        exit 0
    }

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
        $allMarkersCurrent = $true
        foreach ($lang in $languages) {
            $markerPath = Join-Path (Join-Path $registryRoot 'Deployments') $lang.Tag
            $marker = Get-ItemProperty -Path $markerPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            if (
                -not $marker -or
                $marker.Installed -ne 1 -or
                $marker.Version -ne $templateVersion -or
                $marker.ConfigurationId -ne $configurationId
            ) {
                $allMarkersCurrent = $false
            }
        }

        if ($allLanguagesInstalled -and $allSettingsConfigured) {
            if (-not $allMarkersCurrent) {
                # Adopt an already-correct device for Win32 registry detection.
                foreach ($lang in $languages) { Save-DeploymentMarker $lang.Tag }
                Write-Output 'Language pack(s) and device settings were already configured. Win32 deployment markers created.'
            }
            else {
                Write-Output 'Language pack(s) and device settings are already configured. No changes made.'
            }
            exit 0
        }
    }

    foreach ($lang in $languages) {
        if ($installedTags -notcontains $lang.Tag) {
            Write-Output "Installing language pack $($lang.Tag)..."
            Install-Language -Language $lang.Tag  # can take 20-30 min on some builds
            if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
                Write-Output "[CHANGED] Language pack installed: $($lang.Tag)"
            }
        }

        $list = Get-WinUserLanguageList
        if ($list.LanguageTag -notcontains $lang.Tag) {
            $list.Add($lang.Tag)
            Set-WinUserLanguageList -LanguageList $list -Force
        }
        Set-KeyboardLayout $lang
    }

    # Primary language drives UI language, culture, region and timezone.
    Set-SystemPreferredUILanguage -Language $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-WinSystemLocale -SystemLocale $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-WinUILanguageOverride -Language $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-Culture -CultureInfo $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-WinHomeLocation -GeoId $primaryLanguage.GeoId
    Set-TimeZone -Id $primaryLanguage.Timezone
    Copy-UserInternationalSettingsToSystem -WelcomeScreen $true -NewUser $true

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
        Write-Output "[APPLIED] System preferred UI language: $($primaryLanguage.Tag)"
        Write-Output "[APPLIED] System locale: $($primaryLanguage.Tag)"
        Write-Output "[APPLIED] Timezone: $($primaryLanguage.Timezone)"
        Write-Output '[APPLIED] Windows welcome screen and new-user defaults updated'
        Write-Output '[APPLIED] Device completion receipt recorded for user policies'
        Write-Output '[INFO] A restart is required before Windows reports the new system locale - detection can stay non-compliant until the device restarts.'
    }

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
        foreach ($lang in $languages) { Save-DeploymentMarker $lang.Tag }
    }
    else {
        Save-RemediationMarker
    }

    if ($rebootRequested) {
        Write-Output 'Language pack installation completed successfully. A restart or new sign-in is required.'

        if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
            # Win32 maps 3010 to a successful soft reboot request. Intune owns
            # the reboot; never force one from the generated install script.
            exit 3010
        }
        elseif ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
            Write-Output 'Result: Remediated successfully (restart or new sign-in required)'
        }
    }
    else {
        if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
            Write-Output 'Result: Remediated successfully'
        }
        else {
            Write-Output 'Language pack installation completed successfully.'
        }
    }
    exit 0
}
catch {
    Write-Output "Language pack installation failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit 1
}

DescriptionThis Proactive Remediation installs and configures the Dutch (Netherlands) language pack (nl-NL) on supported Windows 11 22H2 and later devices. The script ensures that the Dutch language pack is installed, configured as the primary display language, and applies the required regional settings. Note: This will need the user to reboot the system itself The remediation performs the following actions on Device/system level: Installs the nl-NL language pack using the Windows LanguagePackManagement module. Configures Dutch (nl-NL) as the primary Windows UI language. Sets the system culture and regional format to Dutch (Netherlands). Configures the home location to Netherlands (GeoID 176). Sets the time zone to W. Europe Standard Time. Configures the US-International keyboard layout (00020409) for the Dutch language profile. Copies international settings to the Welcome Screen and new user profiles. Stores the original device language and regional configuration in the registry as a rollback reference. Creates deployment markers in the registry to support Intune detection and reporting. Runs only on supported Windows 11 builds (22621/22H2 or later). Returns success if the desired configuration is already present, making the remediation fully idempotent. Registry Path Used: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\LanguagePackDeployerExpand

Detection Script Content
View script
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Detects the requested Windows language configuration for Intune Remediations.
.DESCRIPTION
    Reads the current device state directly. It does not depend on or create
    LanguagePackDeployer registry markers, so an already-correct device is
    compliant on the first detection run.
.NOTES
    Product: Language Pack Deployer
    Version: 1.0.0

    Exit codes:
      0    The requested device configuration is present
      1    Remediation is required or detection failed

    Detection runs in device context. Settings that belong to an interactive
    user profile, such as keyboard preferences and user culture, are not tested.
#>

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# <LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>
$tags = @('nl-NL')
$primaryTag = 'nl-NL'
$timezone = 'W. Europe Standard Time'
# </LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>

try {
    $installedLanguages = @(Get-InstalledLanguage)
    $issues = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

    Write-Output 'Language Pack Deployer - Device detection'
    Write-Output "Requested languages: $($tags -join ', ')"
    Write-Output "Primary language: $primaryTag"

    foreach ($tag in $tags) {
        if ($installedLanguages.LanguageId -notcontains $tag) {
            $issues.Add("Language pack is not installed: $tag")
            Write-Output "[FAIL] Installed language: $tag"
        }
        else {
            Write-Output "[PASS] Installed language: $tag"
        }
    }

    $actualUiLanguage = Get-SystemPreferredUILanguage
    if ($actualUiLanguage -ne $primaryTag) {
        $issues.Add("System preferred UI language is '$actualUiLanguage'; expected '$primaryTag'")
        Write-Output "[FAIL] System preferred UI language: $actualUiLanguage (expected: $primaryTag)"
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "[PASS] System preferred UI language: $actualUiLanguage"
    }

    $actualSystemLocale = (Get-WinSystemLocale).Name
    if ($actualSystemLocale -ne $primaryTag) {
        $issues.Add("System locale is '$actualSystemLocale'; expected '$primaryTag'")
        Write-Output "[FAIL] System locale: $actualSystemLocale (expected: $primaryTag)"
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "[PASS] System locale: $actualSystemLocale"
    }

    $actualTimezone = (Get-TimeZone).Id
    if ($actualTimezone -ne $timezone) {
        $issues.Add("Timezone is '$actualTimezone'; expected '$timezone'")
        Write-Output "[FAIL] Timezone: $actualTimezone (expected: $timezone)"
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "[PASS] Timezone: $actualTimezone"
    }

    if ($issues.Count -gt 0) {
        Write-Output "Result: Non-compliant ($($issues.Count) issue(s))"
        foreach ($issue in $issues) {
            Write-Output " - $issue"
        }
        exit 1
    }

    Write-Output 'Result: Compliant (all device checks passed)'
    exit 0
}
catch {
    Write-Output "Language configuration detection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit 1
}
Remediation Script Content
View script
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Installs and configures one or more Windows language packs.
.DESCRIPTION
    Ensures that the requested language packs are installed and applies the
    selected primary language and regional settings. Win32 deployments also
    record state for their registry-based Intune detection rules.

    The script is safe to run repeatedly. Existing language packs are reused,
    and settings that are already correct are left unchanged.
.NOTES
    Product:      Language Pack Deployer
    Version:      1.0.0
    Requirements: Windows 11 22H2 or later
                  64-bit Windows PowerShell
                  Administrator or SYSTEM context

    Exit codes:
      0    Success or already configured
      1    Installation or configuration failed
      3010 Success with restart required (Win32 deployments only)

    Intune Remediations and platform scripts always return 0 after a successful
    run, including when a restart or new sign-in is required. This script never
    forces a restart.
#>

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$registryRoot = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\LanguagePackDeployer'
$templateVersion = '1.0.0'

# <LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>
$languages = @(
    @{ Tag = 'nl-NL'; GeoId = 176; Timezone = 'W. Europe Standard Time'; Keyboard = '00020409'; KeyboardName = 'US-International' }
)
$primaryTag = 'nl-NL'
$rebootRequested = $false
$deploymentTarget = 'remediation'
$configurationId = 'cfg-v1-0ab33f18'
# </LanguagePackDeployerConfiguration>

# --- 64-bit guard: IME is 32-bit; language modules need 64-bit PowerShell ---
if ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 -eq 'AMD64') {
    $sysnative = "$env:WINDIR\sysnative\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe"
    & $sysnative -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

# --- OS guard: Install-Language requires Windows 11 22H2+ ---
$build = [System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version.Build
if ($build -lt 22621) {
    Write-Output "Unsupported OS build $build - Install-Language requires Windows 11 22H2 (build 22621) or later."
    exit 1
}

if ($deploymentTarget -notin @('win32', 'remediation', 'platformScript')) {
    Write-Output "Unsupported deployment target: $deploymentTarget"
    exit 1
}

function Save-OriginalState {
    # Preserve the original state once so the final uninstall can restore it.
    if (Get-ItemProperty -Path $registryRoot -Name 'OriginalState' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { return }
    $state = @{
        languageList = @((Get-WinUserLanguageList).LanguageTag)
        culture      = (Get-Culture).Name
        geoId        = (Get-WinHomeLocation).GeoId
        timezone     = (Get-TimeZone).Id
        systemLocale = (Get-WinSystemLocale).Name
        systemPreferredLanguage = (Get-SystemPreferredUILanguage)
        capturedAt   = (Get-Date).ToString('o')
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
    New-Item -Path $registryRoot -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $registryRoot -Name 'OriginalState' -Value $state -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
}

function Save-DeploymentMarker([string]$tag) {
    $key = Join-Path (Join-Path $registryRoot 'Deployments') $tag
    New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Installed' -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Version' -Value $templateVersion -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'ConfigurationId' -Value $configurationId -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Timestamp' -Value (Get-Date).ToString('o') -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
}

function Save-RemediationMarker {
    $key = Join-Path $registryRoot 'Remediation'

    New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null

    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Completed' -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Version' -Value $templateVersion -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'ConfigurationId' -Value $configurationId -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'Timestamp' -Value (Get-Date).ToString('o') -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
}

function Get-KeyboardTip([hashtable]$lang) {
    # InputMethodTip format: "<LCID hex>:<KLID>", e.g. 0413:00020409 = Dutch + US-International.
    if (-not $lang.Keyboard) { return $null }
    $lcidHex = '{0:x4}' -f ([System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::GetCultureInfo($lang.Tag).LCID)
    return "${lcidHex}:$($lang.Keyboard)"
}

function Set-KeyboardLayout([hashtable]$lang) {
    $tip = Get-KeyboardTip $lang
    if (-not $tip) { return }
    $list = Get-WinUserLanguageList
    $entry = $list | Where-Object { $_.LanguageTag -eq $lang.Tag }
    if ($entry -and ($entry.InputMethodTips -notcontains $tip)) {
        $entry.InputMethodTips.Clear()
        $entry.InputMethodTips.Add($tip) | Out-Null
        Set-WinUserLanguageList -LanguageList $list -Force
    }
}

function Test-CurrentAccountSettings([hashtable]$lang, [bool]$isPrimary) {
    # Under the recommended SYSTEM context these values are the source copied
    # to the welcome screen and defaults for new users. They do not represent
    # an already signed-in interactive user's profile.
    $list = Get-WinUserLanguageList
    $entry = $list | Where-Object { $_.LanguageTag -eq $lang.Tag }
    if (-not $entry) { return $false }
    $tip = Get-KeyboardTip $lang
    if ($tip -and ($entry.InputMethodTips -notcontains $tip)) { return $false }
    if ($isPrimary) {
        if ((Get-Culture).Name -ne $lang.Tag) { return $false }
        if ((Get-WinHomeLocation).GeoId -ne $lang.GeoId) { return $false }
    }
    return $true
}

try {
    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
        Save-OriginalState
    }

    $installedTags = @((Get-InstalledLanguage).LanguageId)
    $allLanguagesInstalled = $true
    foreach ($lang in $languages) {
        if ($installedTags -notcontains $lang.Tag) { $allLanguagesInstalled = $false }
    }

    $primaryLanguage = $languages | Where-Object { $_.Tag -eq $primaryTag }
    $deviceSettingsConfigured = (
        (Get-SystemPreferredUILanguage) -eq $primaryTag -and
        (Get-WinSystemLocale).Name -eq $primaryTag -and
        (Get-TimeZone).Id -eq $primaryLanguage.Timezone
    )
    $currentAccountSettingsConfigured = $true
    foreach ($lang in $languages) {
        if (-not (Test-CurrentAccountSettings $lang ($lang.Tag -eq $primaryTag))) {
            $currentAccountSettingsConfigured = $false
        }
    }
    $allSettingsConfigured = $deviceSettingsConfigured -and $currentAccountSettingsConfigured

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
        Write-Output 'Language Pack Deployer - Device remediation'
        Write-Output "Requested languages: $(($languages.Tag) -join ', ')"
        Write-Output "Primary language: $primaryTag"
        Write-Output "Timezone: $($primaryLanguage.Timezone)"
        foreach ($lang in $languages) {
            if ($installedTags -contains $lang.Tag) {
                Write-Output "[PASS] Language pack already installed: $($lang.Tag)"
            }
            else {
                Write-Output "[ACTION] Language pack requires installation: $($lang.Tag)"
            }
        }
    }

    if ($deploymentTarget -ne 'win32' -and $allLanguagesInstalled -and $allSettingsConfigured) {
        if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
            Write-Output 'Result: Compliant (no remediation changes were required)'
        }
        else {
            Write-Output 'Language pack(s) and device settings are already configured. No changes made.'
        }
        exit 0
    }

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
        $allMarkersCurrent = $true
        foreach ($lang in $languages) {
            $markerPath = Join-Path (Join-Path $registryRoot 'Deployments') $lang.Tag
            $marker = Get-ItemProperty -Path $markerPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            if (
                -not $marker -or
                $marker.Installed -ne 1 -or
                $marker.Version -ne $templateVersion -or
                $marker.ConfigurationId -ne $configurationId
            ) {
                $allMarkersCurrent = $false
            }
        }

        if ($allLanguagesInstalled -and $allSettingsConfigured) {
            if (-not $allMarkersCurrent) {
                # Adopt an already-correct device for Win32 registry detection.
                foreach ($lang in $languages) { Save-DeploymentMarker $lang.Tag }
                Write-Output 'Language pack(s) and device settings were already configured. Win32 deployment markers created.'
            }
            else {
                Write-Output 'Language pack(s) and device settings are already configured. No changes made.'
            }
            exit 0
        }
    }

    foreach ($lang in $languages) {
        if ($installedTags -notcontains $lang.Tag) {
            Write-Output "Installing language pack $($lang.Tag)..."
            Install-Language -Language $lang.Tag  # can take 20-30 min on some builds
            if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
                Write-Output "[CHANGED] Language pack installed: $($lang.Tag)"
            }
        }

        $list = Get-WinUserLanguageList
        if ($list.LanguageTag -notcontains $lang.Tag) {
            $list.Add($lang.Tag)
            Set-WinUserLanguageList -LanguageList $list -Force
        }
        Set-KeyboardLayout $lang
    }

    # Primary language drives UI language, culture, region and timezone.
    Set-SystemPreferredUILanguage -Language $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-WinSystemLocale -SystemLocale $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-WinUILanguageOverride -Language $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-Culture -CultureInfo $primaryLanguage.Tag
    Set-WinHomeLocation -GeoId $primaryLanguage.GeoId
    Set-TimeZone -Id $primaryLanguage.Timezone
    Copy-UserInternationalSettingsToSystem -WelcomeScreen $true -NewUser $true

if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
    Save-RemediationMarker
}

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
        Write-Output "[APPLIED] System preferred UI language: $($primaryLanguage.Tag)"
        Write-Output "[APPLIED] System locale: $($primaryLanguage.Tag)"
        Write-Output "[APPLIED] Timezone: $($primaryLanguage.Timezone)"
        Write-Output '[APPLIED] Windows welcome screen and new-user defaults updated'
    }

    if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
        foreach ($lang in $languages) { Save-DeploymentMarker $lang.Tag }
    }

    if ($rebootRequested) {
        Write-Output 'Language pack installation completed successfully. A restart or new sign-in is required.'

        if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'win32') {
            # Win32 maps 3010 to a successful soft reboot request. Intune owns
            # the reboot; never force one from the generated install script.
            exit 3010
        }
        elseif ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
            Write-Output 'Result: Remediated successfully (restart or new sign-in required)'
        }
    }
    else {
        if ($deploymentTarget -eq 'remediation') {
            Write-Output 'Result: Remediated successfully'
        }
        else {
            Write-Output 'Language pack installation completed successfully.'
        }
    }
    exit 0
}
catch {
    Write-Output "Language pack installation failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit 1
}

Detection Script Content
View script
﻿<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Script to detect HP Bloatware via Intune Proactive Remediations.

    .DESCRIPTION
    This script contains code which can be used to detect HP OEM software (Win32, Appx & Provisioned). 
    Detections are logged locally in the log folder: C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs\

    .CREDITS
    written by: Jeffrey Bouwmeester
    
    .NOTES
    Name    : RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-HPBloatware-detect.ps1
    Intune Proactive Remediation - Detection Script.
    Exits with code 1 if HP bloatware is found (triggering remediation). Exits with code 0 if the system is clean.

    .DETAILS
    Creation Date:  2026-06-01
    Version history:
        1.0.0 - (2026-06-01) - Jeffrey Bouwmeester - Script released
        1.2.0 - (2026-06-11) - Chris Koopman - Added AppxPackage detection logic and implemented advanced daily custom logging.
        1.3.0 - (2026-06-17) - Chris Koopman - Optimized for performance (Lean & Mean), added Appx/Provisioned logic, English logging.
        1.4.0 - (2026-06-25) - Chris Koopman - Split logic to exclusively target HP vendor bloatware.

    .EXECUTION (manual)
    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass
    .\RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-HPBloatware-detect.ps1
#>

$appName = "HPBloatware"
$LogFolder = "C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs"
$Timestampdaily = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
$pattern = "HP Wolf|HP Sure|HP Security|HP Connection Optimizer|HP Documentation|HPSystemInformation|HPAudioControl|myHP"
$paths = "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*", "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
$foundApps = @()

# --- Helper Functions ---
function Write-CustomLog([string]$Message, [string]$LogType = 'Detect') {
    if (-not (Test-Path $LogFolder)) { New-Item $LogFolder -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null }
    "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_THHmmss') - $Message" | Out-File -FilePath "$LogFolder\${appName}_${LogType}_${Timestampdaily}.log" -Append
}

function Rotate-CustomLogs([string]$Filter) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $LogFolder -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | 
        Sort-Object CreationTime -Descending | Select-Object -Skip 5 | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

# --- Initialize & Clean Logs ---
Rotate-CustomLogs -Filter "${appName}_Detect_*.log"
Write-CustomLog -Message " "
Write-CustomLog -Message "=== START DETECTION ==="

# --- Detect Win32 Apps ---
$win32Apps = (Get-ItemProperty $paths -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).DisplayName | Where-Object { $_ -match $pattern } | Select-Object -Unique
foreach ($app in $win32Apps) {
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Detected: $app"
    $foundApps += $app
}

# --- Detect Appx Packages ---
$appxApps = (Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Name | Where-Object { $_ -match $pattern } | Select-Object -Unique
foreach ($app in $appxApps) {
    if ($foundApps -notcontains $app) {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Detected Appx: $app"
        $foundApps += $app
    }
}

# --- Detect Provisioned Appx Packages ---
$provApps = Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match $pattern -or $_.PackageName -match $pattern }
foreach ($prov in $provApps) {
    $name = if ($prov.DisplayName) { $prov.DisplayName } else { $prov.PackageName }
    if ($foundApps -notcontains $name) {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Detected Provisioned Appx: $name"
        $foundApps += $name
    }
}

# --- Intune Output & Exit ---
if ($foundApps.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Output "Found: $($foundApps -join ', ')"
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Bloatware FOUND"
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Summary: $($foundApps -join ', ')"
    exit 1
} else {
    Write-Output "No bloatware found"
    Write-CustomLog -Message "No bloatware found"
    exit 0
}
Remediation Script Content
View script
﻿<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Script to remove HP Bloatware via Intune Proactive Remediations.

    .DESCRIPTION
    This script contains code which can be used to aggressively remove HP OEM software (Win32, Appx & Provisioned).
    It stops related processes, uninstalls applications, disables services and scheduled tasks, and blocks the HP Support Assistant.
    Actions are logged locally in the log folder: C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs\

    .CREDITS
    written by: Jeffrey Bouwmeester
    
    .NOTES
    Name    : RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-HPBloatware-remediation.ps1
    Intune Proactive Remediation - Remediation Script.
    Note: May require multiple runs due to service locks. Only outputs final status for Intune capturing.

    .DETAILS
    Creation Date:  2026-06-01
    Version history:
        1.0.0 - (2026-06-01) - Jeffrey Bouwmeester - Script released
        1.2.0 - (2026-06-11) - Chris Koopman - Added AppxPackage logic, advanced logging, silenced cmdlet errors, isolated tasks to HP Wolf presence, and included wscsvc lock-bypass.
        1.3.0 - (2026-06-17) - Chris Koopman - Optimized (Lean & Mean), added AppxPackage/Provisioned fallback logic based on PackageName.
        1.4.0 - (2026-06-25) - Chris Koopman - Split logic to exclusively target HP vendor bloatware.

    .EXECUTION (manual)
    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass
    .\RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-HPBloatware-remediation.ps1
#>

$appName = "HPBloatware"
$LogFolder = "C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs"
$Timestampdaily = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
$pattern = "HP Wolf|HP Sure|HP Security|HP Connection Optimizer|HP Documentation|HPSystemInformation|HPAudioControl|myHP"
$paths = "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*", "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"

$removedApps = @()
$failedApps  = @()
$wolfFound   = $false

# --- Helper Functions ---
function Write-CustomLog([string]$Message, [string]$LogType = 'Remediation') {
    if (-not (Test-Path $LogFolder)) { New-Item $LogFolder -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null }
    "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_THHmmss') - $Message" | Out-File -FilePath "$LogFolder\${appName}_${LogType}_${Timestampdaily}.log" -Append
}

function Rotate-CustomLogs([string]$Filter) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $LogFolder -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | 
        Sort-Object CreationTime -Descending | Select-Object -Skip 5 | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

# --- Initialize Logging ---
Rotate-CustomLogs -Filter "${appName}_Remediation_*.log"
Write-CustomLog -Message " "
Write-CustomLog -Message "===== START HP CLEANUP ====="

# 1. Stop Processen
Write-CustomLog -Message "Stopping related processes"
Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match "^hp|wolf|^sure" } | ForEach-Object {
    if ($_.Name -match "wolf|^sure") { $wolfFound = $true }
    Stop-Process $_ -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Stopped process: $($_.Name)"
}

# 2. Uninstall Win32 Apps
Get-ItemProperty $paths -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match $pattern -and $_.UninstallString } | ForEach-Object {
    $name = $_.DisplayName
    $uninstall = $_.UninstallString

    if ($name -match "Wolf|Sure") { $wolfFound = $true }
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Uninstalling: $name"

    if ($uninstall -match "msiexec") {
        $uninstall = $uninstall -replace "/I", "/X"
        if ($uninstall -notmatch "/qn") { $uninstall += " /qn /norestart" }
    }

    $success = $false
    for ($i = 1; $i -le 3; $i++) {
        try {
            Start-Process "cmd.exe" -ArgumentList "/c $uninstall" -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait -ErrorAction Stop
            Write-CustomLog -Message "SUCCESS ($i): $name"
            $success = $true
            break
        } catch {
            Write-CustomLog -Message "FAILED ($i): $name"
            Start-Sleep 5
        }
    }

    if ($success) { if ($removedApps -notcontains $name) { $removedApps += $name } } 
    else { if ($failedApps -notcontains $name) { $failedApps += $name } }
}

# 3. Services Uitschakelen
Write-CustomLog -Message "Processing services"
Get-Service -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match "^hp|wolf|^sure|security" -or $_.DisplayName -match "^hp|wolf|^sure|security" } | ForEach-Object {
    if ($_.Name -match "wolf|^sure" -or $_.DisplayName -match "wolf|^sure") { $wolfFound = $true }
    Stop-Service $_.Name -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Set-Service $_.Name -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Actioned service: $($_.Name)"
}

# 4. Scheduled Tasks Uitschakelen (Alleen bij Wolf/Sure)
if ($wolfFound) {
    Write-CustomLog -Message "HP Wolf/Sure detected. Disabling related scheduled tasks."
    Get-ScheduledTask -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -match "^HP|Wolf|^Sure" } | ForEach-Object {
        Disable-ScheduledTask -TaskPath $_.TaskPath -TaskName $_.TaskName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Disabled task: $($_.TaskName)"
    }
}

# 5. HP Support Assistant Blokkeren
Write-CustomLog -Message "Blocking HP Support Assistant paths"
"C:\Program Files (x86)\HP\HP Support Framework", "C:\Program Files\HP\HP Support Framework" | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | ForEach-Object {
    Rename-Item $_ "$_.disabled" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Disabled path: $_"
}

# 6. AppxPackages Verwijderen
Write-CustomLog -Message "Removing Appx Packages"
Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match $pattern } | ForEach-Object {
    $name = $_.Name
    try {
        Remove-AppxPackage -Package $_.PackageFullName -AllUsers -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Uninstalled Appx: $name"
        if ($removedApps -notcontains $name) { $removedApps += $name }
    } catch {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Failed Appx: $name"
        if ($failedApps -notcontains $name) { $failedApps += $name }
    }
}

# 7. ProvisionedPackages Verwijderen
Write-CustomLog -Message "Removing Provisioned Packages"
Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match $pattern -or $_.PackageName -match $pattern } | ForEach-Object {
    $name = if ($_.DisplayName) { $_.DisplayName } else { $_.PackageName }
    try {
        Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -PackageName $_.PackageName -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Uninstalled Provisioned Appx: $name"
        if ($removedApps -notcontains $name) { $removedApps += $name }
    } catch {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Failed Provisioned Appx: $name"
        if ($failedApps -notcontains $name) { $failedApps += $name }
    }
}

Write-CustomLog -Message "===== HP CLEANUP COMPLETE ====="

# --- Intune Output ---
if ($removedApps.Count -gt 0 -and $failedApps.Count -eq 0) { Write-Output "Removed: $($removedApps -join ', ')" }
elseif ($removedApps.Count -gt 0 -and $failedApps.Count -gt 0) { Write-Output "Removed: $($removedApps -join ', ') | Failed: $($failedApps -join ', ')" }
elseif ($failedApps.Count -gt 0) { Write-Output "Failed: $($failedApps -join ', ')" }
else { Write-Output "Removed: none" }

exit 0

﻿<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Script to detect Windows Bloatware via Intune Proactive Remediations.

    .DESCRIPTION
    This script contains code which can be used to detect Windows OS bloatware (Win32, Appx & Provisioned). 
    Detections are logged locally in the log folder: C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs\

    .CREDITS
    written by: Jeffrey Bouwmeester
    
    .NOTES
    Name    : RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-WinBloatware-detect.ps1
    Intune Proactive Remediation - Detection Script.
    Exits with code 1 if Windows bloatware is found (triggering remediation). Exits with code 0 if the system is clean.

    .DETAILS
    Creation Date:  2026-06-25
    Version history:
        1.0.0 - (2026-06-25) - Chris Koopman - Script released

    .EXECUTION (manual)
    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass
    .\RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-WinBloatware-detect.ps1
#>

$appName = "WinBloatware"
$LogFolder = "C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs"
$Timestampdaily = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
$pattern = "MicrosoftSolitaireCollection|MicrosoftFamily|XboxGameOverlay|XboxIdentityProvider|XboxSpeechToTextOverlay|Xbox\.TCUI|DevHome|MicrosoftOfficeHub|YourPhone|CrossDevice|IntelConnectivityPerformanceSuite"
$paths = "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*", "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
$foundApps = @()

# --- Helper Functions ---
function Write-CustomLog([string]$Message, [string]$LogType = 'Detect') {
    if (-not (Test-Path $LogFolder)) { New-Item $LogFolder -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null }
    "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_THHmmss') - $Message" | Out-File -FilePath "$LogFolder\${appName}_${LogType}_${Timestampdaily}.log" -Append
}

function Rotate-CustomLogs([string]$Filter) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $LogFolder -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | 
        Sort-Object CreationTime -Descending | Select-Object -Skip 5 | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

# --- Initialize & Clean Logs ---
Rotate-CustomLogs -Filter "${appName}_Detect_*.log"
Write-CustomLog -Message " "
Write-CustomLog -Message "=== START DETECTION ==="

# --- Detect Win32 Apps ---
$win32Apps = (Get-ItemProperty $paths -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).DisplayName | Where-Object { $_ -match $pattern } | Select-Object -Unique
foreach ($app in $win32Apps) {
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Detected: $app"
    $foundApps += $app
}

# --- Detect Appx Packages ---
$appxApps = (Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Name | Where-Object { $_ -match $pattern } | Select-Object -Unique
foreach ($app in $appxApps) {
    if ($foundApps -notcontains $app) {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Detected Appx: $app"
        $foundApps += $app
    }
}

# --- Detect Provisioned Appx Packages ---
$provApps = Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match $pattern -or $_.PackageName -match $pattern }
foreach ($prov in $provApps) {
    $name = if ($prov.DisplayName) { $prov.DisplayName } else { $prov.PackageName }
    if ($foundApps -notcontains $name) {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Detected Provisioned Appx: $name"
        $foundApps += $name
    }
}

# --- Intune Output & Exit ---
if ($foundApps.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Output "Found: $($foundApps -join ', ')"
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Bloatware FOUND"
    Write-CustomLog -Message "Summary: $($foundApps -join ', ')"
    exit 1
} else {
    Write-Output "No bloatware found"
    Write-CustomLog -Message "No bloatware found"
    exit 0
}

<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Script to remove Windows Bloatware via Intune Proactive Remediations.

    .DESCRIPTION
    This script contains code which can be used to aggressively remove Windows OS bloatware (Win32, Appx & Provisioned).
    Actions are logged locally in the log folder: C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs\

    .CREDITS
    written by: Chris Koopman
    
    .NOTES
    Name    : RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-WinBloatware-remediation.ps1
    Intune Proactive Remediation - Remediation Script.

    .DETAILS
    Creation Date:  2026-06-25
    Version history:
        1.0.0 - (2026-06-25) - Chris Koopman - Script released

    .EXECUTION (manual)
    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass
    .\RS-ITQ-da-win-all-Remove-WinBloatware-remediation.ps1
#>

$appName = "WinBloatware"
$LogFolder = "C:\ProgramData\IntuneLogs"
$Timestampdaily = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
$pattern = "MicrosoftSolitaireCollection|MicrosoftFamily|XboxGameOverlay|XboxIdentityProvider|XboxSpeechToTextOverlay|Xbox\.TCUI|DevHome|MicrosoftOfficeHub|YourPhone|CrossDevice|IntelConnectivityPerformanceSuite"
$paths = "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*", "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"

$removedApps = @()
$failedApps  = @()

# --- Helper Functions ---
function Write-CustomLog([string]$Message, [string]$LogType = 'Remediation') {
    if (-not (Test-Path $LogFolder)) { New-Item $LogFolder -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null }
    "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_THHmmss') - $Message" | Out-File -FilePath "$LogFolder\${appName}_${LogType}_${Timestampdaily}.log" -Append
}

function Rotate-CustomLogs([string]$Filter) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $LogFolder -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | 
        Sort-Object CreationTime -Descending | Select-Object -Skip 5 | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

# --- Initialize Logging ---
Rotate-CustomLogs -Filter "${appName}_Remediation_*.log"
Write-CustomLog -Message " "
Write-CustomLog -Message "===== START WINDOWS BLOATWARE CLEANUP ====="

# 1. Uninstall Win32 Apps
Get-ItemProperty $paths -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match $pattern -and $_.UninstallString } | ForEach-Object {
    $name = $_.DisplayName
    $uninstall = $_.UninstallString

    Write-CustomLog -Message "Uninstalling: $name"

    if ($uninstall -match "msiexec") {
        $uninstall = $uninstall -replace "/I", "/X"
        if ($uninstall -notmatch "/qn") { $uninstall += " /qn /norestart" }
    }

    $success = $false
    for ($i = 1; $i -le 3; $i++) {
        try {
            Start-Process "cmd.exe" -ArgumentList "/c $uninstall" -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait -ErrorAction Stop
            Write-CustomLog -Message "SUCCESS ($i): $name"
            $success = $true
            break
        } catch {
            Write-CustomLog -Message "FAILED ($i): $name"
            Start-Sleep 5
        }
    }

    if ($success) { if ($removedApps -notcontains $name) { $removedApps += $name } } 
    else { if ($failedApps -notcontains $name) { $failedApps += $name } }
}

# 2. AppxPackages Verwijderen
Write-CustomLog -Message "Removing Appx Packages"
Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match $pattern } | ForEach-Object {
    $name = $_.Name
    try {
        Remove-AppxPackage -Package $_.PackageFullName -AllUsers -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Uninstalled Appx: $name"
        if ($removedApps -notcontains $name) { $removedApps += $name }
    } catch {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Failed Appx: $name"
        if ($failedApps -notcontains $name) { $failedApps += $name }
    }
}

# 3. ProvisionedPackages Verwijderen
Write-CustomLog -Message "Removing Provisioned Packages"
Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match $pattern -or $_.PackageName -match $pattern } | ForEach-Object {
    $name = if ($_.DisplayName) { $_.DisplayName } else { $_.PackageName }
    try {
        Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -PackageName $_.PackageName -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Uninstalled Provisioned Appx: $name"
        if ($removedApps -notcontains $name) { $removedApps += $name }
    } catch {
        Write-CustomLog -Message "Failed Provisioned Appx: $name"
        if ($failedApps -notcontains $name) { $failedApps += $name }
    }
}

Write-CustomLog -Message "===== WINDOWS BLOATWARE CLEANUP COMPLETE ====="

# --- Intune Output ---
if ($removedApps.Count -gt 0 -and $failedApps.Count -eq 0) { Write-Output "Removed: $($removedApps -join ', ')" }
elseif ($removedApps.Count -gt 0 -and $failedApps.Count -gt 0) { Write-Output "Removed: $($removedApps -join ', ') | Failed: $($failedApps -join ', ')" }
elseif ($failedApps.Count -gt 0) { Write-Output "Failed: $($failedApps -join ', ')" }
else { Write-Output "Removed: none" }

exit 0

﻿<#
.SYNOPSIS
    This detection script checks if a Dell device has SecureBoot enabled, and if SecureBoot is disable it will check if a BIOS password is set.

.DESCRIPTION
    The script can have the need to uses the DellBIOSProvider module to get the status of the BIOS password feature.
    If a BIOS password is set, SecureBoot cannot be enabled by the remediation and the script exits with a status code of 0.
    
    DellBIOSProvider module can only be installed if VC++ Redistributable is installed, so this is checked also.

.NOTES
    Filename: PRS-BASE-DG-Default-Remediation_SecureBootDell-detection.ps1
    Version: 2.0
    Date: 2025-07-03
    Author : Chris Koopman
#>

#######################
### START FUNCTIONS ###
#######################

# Function: Check if VC++ Runtime is installed
function Test-VCRuntimeInstalled {
    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\VisualStudio\14.0\VC\Runtimes\x64'
    if (Test-Path $key) {
        $installed = Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name Installed -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        return ($installed.Installed -eq 1)
    }
    return $false
}

# Function: Install VC++ Runtime
function Install-VCRuntime {
    $vcUrl = "https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe"
    $vcInstaller = "$env:TEMP\vc_redist.x64.exe"
    Write-Output "Downloading VC++ Redistributable..."
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $vcUrl -OutFile $vcInstaller -UseBasicParsing
    Write-Output "Installing VC++ Redistributable..."
    Start-Process -FilePath $vcInstaller -ArgumentList "/install", "/quiet", "/norestart" -Wait
    Remove-Item $vcInstaller -Force
}

# Function to detect if module is installed and import or install it
function Load-Module {
    param([string]$m)

    if (Get-Module | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $m }) {
        Write-Output "Module $m is already imported."
    }
    elseif (Get-Module -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $m }) {
        Write-Output "Importing Module $m"
        Import-Module $m -Verbose
    }
    else {

        # For the module DellBIOSProvider is VC++ Runtime needed to be installed, so check if installed
        if (-not (Test-VCRuntimeInstalled)) {
        Write-Output "Installing VC++ Runtime"
        Install-VCRuntime
        }
        else {
        Write-Output "VC++ Runtime already installed"
        }
       
        # PackageProvider NuGet is needed, always install to ensure the latest version is installed.
        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -Force -Scope CurrentUser -Confirm:$false

        # Continue to install or load DellBIOSProvider 
        if (Find-Module -Name $m) {
            Write-Output "Installing and importing Module $m"
            Install-Module -Name $m -Force -Scope CurrentUser
            Import-Module $m -Verbose
        }
        else {
            Write-Output "Module $m not found in online gallery, exiting."
        }
    }
}

#####################
### END FUNCTIONS ###
#####################

# Define flag file
$FlagFile = "C:\TEMP\SecureBootEnabled.txt"

# Check manufacturer
$manufacturer = (Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_ComputerSystem).Manufacturer

if ($manufacturer -notlike "*Dell*") { 
    Write-Output "Not a Dell device. Skipping remediation." 
    exit 0
}

# Try getting Secure Boot status
try {
    $secureboot = Confirm-SecureBootUEFI
} catch {
    Write-Output "Secure Boot not supported or UEFI not accessible."
    exit 0
}

# Check Secure Boot is enabled and does the FlagFile exist. If Secureboot is enabled no other check is needed anymore. (exit 0)
if ($secureboot -eq $true) {
    if (Test-Path $FlagFile) {
        try {
            Remove-Item -Path $FlagFile -Force
            Write-Output "Secure Boot is already enabled. Removed flag file: $FlagFile"
        } catch {
            Write-Output "Secure Boot enabled, but failed to remove flag file: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        }
    } else {
        Write-Output "Secure Boot is already enabled."
    }
    exit 0
}

# Still running so Check Secure Boot is disabled, we need to check if BIOS password is set, therefore we need to load DellBIOSProvider provider.
try {
    Load-Module -m "DellBIOSProvider"
    Write-Output "DellBIOSProvider module loaded."
} catch {
    Write-Output "Failed to load DellBIOSProvider module: $($_.Exception.Message)"
}


# Check BIOS password status
$biosPasswordProtected = $false
try {
    $biosPwdStatus = Get-Item -Path "DellSmbios:\Security\IsAdminPasswordSet" -ErrorAction Stop
    if ($biosPwdStatus.CurrentValue -eq $true) {
        $biosPasswordProtected = $true
        Write-Output "BIOS is password protected."
    } else {
        Write-Output "BIOS password is not enabled."
    }
} catch {
    Write-Output "Error reading BIOS password status: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit 0
}

# Check: Skip remediation if BIOS password protected
if ($secureboot -eq $false -and $biosPasswordProtected -eq $true) {
    Write-Output "Secure Boot is disabled, but BIOS is password protected. Skipping remediation."
    exit 0
}

# Check: Skip remediation if Secure Boot still disabled + flag file exists: remediation pending
if ((Test-Path $FlagFile) -and ($secureboot -eq $false)) {
    Write-Output "Secure Boot still disabled, but flag file exists. Reboot likely pending."
    exit 0
}

# Check: Start remediation if Secure Boot disabled and no BIOS password and no flag : remediation needed
if ($secureboot -eq $false -and $biosPasswordProtected -eq $false -and (Test-Path $FlagFile) -eq $false) {
Write-Output "Secure Boot is disabled on a Dell system. Remediation required."
exit 1
}

﻿<#
.SYNOPSIS
    This remediation script change a Dell device to SecureBoot enabled, if no BIOS password is set.

.DESCRIPTION
    The detection script has already checked and installed all nessacary modules and software to control the BIOS setup (because of the need to check if a BIOS password is set).
    The Dell device should be able to change the secureboot BIOS setting to enabled.
   
.NOTES
    Filename: PRS-BASE-DG-Default-Remediation_SecureBootDell-remediation.ps1
    Version: 2.0
    Date: 2025-07-03
    Author : Chris Koopman
#>

#######################
### START FUNCTIONS ###
#######################

# Function: Check if VC++ Runtime is installed
function Test-VCRuntimeInstalled {
    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\VisualStudio\14.0\VC\Runtimes\x64'
    if (Test-Path $key) {
        $installed = Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name Installed -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        return ($installed.Installed -eq 1)
    }
    return $false
}

# Function: Install VC++ Runtime
function Install-VCRuntime {
    $vcUrl = "https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe"
    $vcInstaller = "$env:TEMP\vc_redist.x64.exe"
    Write-Output "Downloading VC++ Redistributable..."
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $vcUrl -OutFile $vcInstaller -UseBasicParsing
    Write-Output "Installing VC++ Redistributable..."
    Start-Process -FilePath $vcInstaller -ArgumentList "/install", "/quiet", "/norestart" -Wait
    Remove-Item $vcInstaller -Force
}

# Function to detect if module is installed and import or install it
function Load-Module {
    param([string]$m)

    if (Get-Module | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $m }) {
        Write-Output "Module $m is already imported."
    }
    elseif (Get-Module -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $m }) {
        Write-Output "Importing Module $m"
        Import-Module $m -Verbose
    }
    else {

        # For the module DellBIOSProvider is VC++ Runtime needed to be installed, so check if installed
        if (-not (Test-VCRuntimeInstalled)) {
        Write-Output "Installing VC++ Runtime"
        Install-VCRuntime
        }
        else {
        Write-Output "VC++ Runtime already installed"
        }
       
        # PackageProvider NuGet is needed, always install to ensure the latest version is installed.
        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -Force -Scope CurrentUser -Confirm:$false

        # Continue to install or load DellBIOSProvider 
        if (Find-Module -Name $m) {
            Write-Output "Installing and importing Module $m"
            Install-Module -Name $m -Force -Scope CurrentUser
            Import-Module $m -Verbose
        }
        else {
            Write-Output "Module $m not found in online gallery, exiting."
        }
    }
}

#####################
### END FUNCTIONS ###
#####################

#First load the DellBiosProvider module
try {
    Load-Module -m "DellBIOSProvider"
    Write-Output "DellBIOSProvider module loaded."
} catch {
    Write-Output "Failed to load DellBIOSProvider module: $($_.Exception.Message)"
}

# Enable Secure Boot
$success = $false
try {
    Write-Output "Enabling Secure Boot..."
    Set-Item -Path "DellSmbios:\SecureBoot\SecureBoot" -Value "Enabled" -ErrorAction Stop
    Write-Output "Secure Boot successfully enabled."
    $success = $true
} catch {
    Write-Output "Failed to enable Secure Boot via DellSmbios: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit
}

# Flag for user notification
if ($success) {
    
    # Define flag file
    $FlagFile = "C:\TEMP\SecureBootEnabled.txt"

    try {
        if (-not (Test-Path "C:\TEMP")) {
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\TEMP" -Force | Out-Null
        }
        "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_THHmmss') - Secure Boot has been enabled. Please restart your device to apply changes." | Out-File -FilePath $FlagFile -Encoding UTF8
        Write-Output "User restart FlagFile created at: $FlagFile"
    } catch {
        Write-Output "Unable to create user restart flag: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

exit 0

<#.SYNOPSIS 
Detect if WHfB is configured for a User
 
.DESCRIPTION 
Below script will check and confirm If WHfB is enabled
for a particular current logged-on user 

.NOTES     
        Name       : Detect-WHfB.ps1
        Author     : JEffrey Bouwmeester
        Version    : 1.0.0  
#>

# Get current user SID
$currentUser = [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
$currentUserSid = $currentUser.User.Value

# Registry path for WHfB PIN provider
$PINguid = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Authentication\Credential Providers\{D6886603-9D2F-4EB2-B667-1971041FA96B}"

if (Test-Path $PINguid) {
    $SIDFolders = Get-ChildItem -Path $PINguid -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    foreach ($folder in $SIDFolders) {
        $props = Get-ItemProperty $folder.PSPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

        if ($folder.PSChildName -eq $currentUserSid -and $props.LogonCredsAvailable -eq 1) {
            Write-Output "WHfB configured for current user"
            exit 1
        }
    }
}

Write-Output "WHfB NOT configured for current user"
exit 0

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Reset Windows Hello for Business for current user

.DESCRIPTION
Deletes the WHfB (Hello) container for the logged-on user
using certutil and prepares system for re-enrollment

.NOTES
Name: Reset-WHFB.ps1
Author  : Jeffrey Bouwmeester
Version : 1.1.1
#>

Write-Output "Starting WHfB reset..."

try {
    # Run certutil to delete Hello container
    $process = Start-Process -FilePath "certutil.exe" `
        -ArgumentList "-deleteHelloContainer" `
        -Wait `
        -PassThru `
        -NoNewWindow

    if ($process.ExitCode -eq 0) {
        Write-Output "WHfB container successfully deleted."

        # Small delay to ensure cleanup completes
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

        # Show popup message to user
        Add-Type -AssemblyName PresentationFramework

        $message = @"
Your Windows Hello (PIN/biometrics) has been reset.

Please sign out and sign back in to set it up again.
"@

        [System.Windows.MessageBox]::Show(
            $message,
            "Windows Hello Reset",
            "OK",
            "Information"
        )

        exit 0
    }
    else {
        Write-Output "certutil returned exit code: $($process.ExitCode)"
        exit 1
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Output "Error resetting WHfB: $_"
    exit 1
}

DescriptionIntune Remediation DETECTION script (detection-only, NOTHING is remediated). Detects whether the logged-on user is synchronizing SharePoint / Teams document libraries with the OneDrive for Business client, i.e. MORE than just their own personal OneDrive for Business library.Expand
Created30/06/2026 12:01:36
Modified02/07/2026 08:41:00
ScopeTags0
Settings
SettingValue
PublisherJeffrey Bouwmeester
Detection Script Content
View script
<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Intune Remediation DETECTION script (detection-only, NOTHING is remediated).
    Detects whether the logged-on user is synchronizing SharePoint / Teams document
    libraries with the OneDrive for Business client, i.e. MORE than just their own
    personal OneDrive for Business library.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The set of libraries the OneDrive client is syncing is stored per-user in the
    registry under HKCU:\Software\SyncEngines\Providers\OneDrive\<ScopeId>. Each scope
    has:
        UrlNamespace  - the full SharePoint/OneDrive URL of the synced library
        MountPoint    - the local folder the library is synced to
        LibraryType   - 'mysite'/'personal' for the personal OneDrive for Business
                        library, 'teamsite' (etc.) for SharePoint document libraries.

    A SharePoint library can appear in the registry for two reasons, and
    we only want to flag the second one:
      1. "Add shortcut to OneDrive" - the library shows up as a shortcut INSIDE the
         user's personal OneDrive folder. Its MountPoint is a descendant of the personal
         OneDrive MountPoint, e.g.
             C:\Users\me\OneDrive - Contoso\Marketing - Documents
      2. "Sync" (the separate sync root) - the library gets its own top-level folder
         next to the OneDrive folder, e.g.
             C:\Users\me\Contoso\Marketing - Documents

    Because HKCU is per-user, this MUST run in the logged-on user's context.

    Deploy as an Intune Remediation with:
        Run this script using the logged-on credentials : Yes   (required - HKCU)
        Run script in 64-bit PowerShell                 : Yes
        Enforce script signature check                  : No (unless you sign it)

    Exit 0 = only the personal OneDrive for Business library is synced (nothing flagged)
    Exit 1 = one or more SharePoint/Teams libraries are synced (flagged)

    The flagged site URLs are written as output so Intune stores them as the
    "Pre-remediation detection output"
#>

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$providersRoot = 'HKCU:\Software\SyncEngines\Providers\OneDrive'

# Normalise a path for prefix comparison: trim trailing separators, lower-case.
function Get-NormalizedPath {
    param([string]$Path)
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Path)) { return $null }
    return $Path.TrimEnd('\', '/').ToLowerInvariant()
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $providersRoot)) {
        Write-Output "OneDrive Business sync not configured for this user."
        exit 0
    }

    # Read every sync scope once.
    $scopes = foreach ($scope in (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $providersRoot -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        $props = Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath $scope.PSPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($props.UrlNamespace)) { continue }
        [PSCustomObject]@{
            Url         = $props.UrlNamespace.TrimEnd('/')
            MountPoint  = "$($props.MountPoint)"
            LibraryType = "$($props.LibraryType)"
        }
    }

    # Pass 1: collect the personal OneDrive folder root(s) - shortcuts live underneath these.
    $personalRoots = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new()
    foreach ($s in $scopes) {
        $isPersonal = ($s.LibraryType -in 'mysite', 'personal') -or ($s.Url -match '(?i)-my\.sharepoint\.com/personal/')
        if ($isPersonal) {
            $n = Get-NormalizedPath $s.MountPoint
            if ($n) { [void]$personalRoots.Add($n) }
        }
    }
    # Fallback roots from the user's environment in case the personal scope is shaped oddly.
    foreach ($envRoot in @($env:OneDriveCommercial, $env:OneDrive)) {
        $n = Get-NormalizedPath $envRoot
        if ($n) { [void]$personalRoots.Add($n) }
    }

    # Pass 2: a non-personal scope is a SEPARATE sync only if its MountPoint is NOT under a personal root.
    $extra = foreach ($s in $scopes) {
        $isPersonal = ($s.LibraryType -in 'mysite', 'personal') -or ($s.Url -match '(?i)-my\.sharepoint\.com/personal/')
        if ($isPersonal) { continue }

        $mp = Get-NormalizedPath $s.MountPoint
        $isShortcut = $false
        if ($mp) {
            foreach ($root in $personalRoots) {
                if ($mp -eq $root -or $mp.StartsWith($root + '\')) { $isShortcut = $true; break }
            }
        }
        if ($isShortcut) { continue }   # "Add shortcut to OneDrive" link - not a separate sync

        $s
    }

    $extra = @($extra | Sort-Object Url -Unique)

    if ($extra.Count -eq 0) {
        Write-Output "OK: only personal OneDrive for Business is synced."
        exit 0
    }

    # Compact, Intune-friendly output. Intune only stores the first ~2KB of detection
    # output, so cap the string and append a marker if we had to truncate.
    $joined = ($extra.Url -join ' | ')
    $maxLen = 1800
    if ($joined.Length -gt $maxLen) {
        $joined = $joined.Substring(0, $maxLen) + ' ...[truncated]'
    }
    Write-Output ("EXTRASYNC ({0}): {1}" -f $extra.Count, $joined)
    exit 1
}catch {
    # Surface the error in the output but stay 'compliant' so we never trigger remediation.
    Write-Output "ERROR: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    exit 0
}
